Rashi on Menachot 89b:10:1.english: Rather, Abaye said: Where their flour and oil have already been burned - of the bulls and rams, as required.

Rashi on Menachot 89b:10:2.english: One may also mix wine — [This is permitted] ab initio, since there is no concern that one might come to mix their flour and oil, which are subject to burning [on the altar], and there is [a prohibition] based on [the verse] "and he shall burn" — that one should not mix fats with fats — since they are already mixed and standing [ready to be burned]. But if their flour and oil have not been burned, one may not mix [the wine], for we are concerned that one might come to mix flour and oil ab initio, which is forbidden, [lest one violate] "that one should not mix fats with fats." And that which the baraita teaches, "but wine one may mix" — that refers to [a case] where their flour and oil have been burned. And that which the middle clause of the Mishnah teaches, "but one may not mix" — that refers to where their flour and oil have not been mixed.

Rashi on Menachot 89b:11:1.english: Even though its meal-offering is doubled - As it is written: "and their meal-offering [shall be] two tenths [of an ephah]" — whereas the other lambs have only one tenth per lamb.

Rashi on Menachot 89b:11:2.english: Its libations were not doubled - Rather, [it had only] three log of wine and three log of oil.

Rashi on Menachot 89b:11:3.english: It taught regarding the lamb - That is to say, it taught regarding this offering what it did not teach regarding all [other] offerings.

Rashi on Menachot 89b:12:1.english: That is mixed with its meal-offering - Its flour [i.e., the meal-offering of the lamb of the Omer] is doubled, so its oil should likewise be doubled.

Rashi on Menachot 89b:13:1.english: What is the biblical derivation? - How is it implied from "and its libation" (וְנִסְכּוֹ) that its oil is not doubled?

Rashi on Menachot 89b:14:1.english: The libation of a meal-offering - that is, [its] oil, [which is] like the libation of a lamb - that is, wine.

Rashi on Menachot 89b:15:1.hebrew: טעון נסכים - כמו שאם שחטו לשמן, ולהכי נקט אשם מצורע, דאילו אשם דעלמא אם שחטו שלא לשמן קרב בלא נסכים כדמעיקרא, אבל אשם מצורע דטעון נסכים איצטריך למימר דכי שחטו שלא לשמן טעון נסכים:
Rashi on Menachot 89b:15:1.english: Requires libations - Just as when it is slaughtered for its own sake [it requires libations]. And this is why [the ruling] specifies the asham metzora: for a regular asham, if slaughtered not for its own sake, it is offered without libations, as was already the case from the outset. But the asham metzora, which requires libations [even when slaughtered for its sake], it was necessary to state that when slaughtered not for its sake, it still requires libations.

Rashi on Menachot 89b:15:2.english: For if you do not say so - [that it requires libations,] he would offer it without libations.

Rashi on Menachot 89b:15:3.hebrew: פסלתו - מליקרב ע"ג המזבח, דלמצורע לא חזי, שהרי נשחט שלא לשמו; ולעולה לא חזי, שהרי לא ניתק לרעייה, ואין ראוי לנדבה, דאשם לא אתי בנדבה. אבל נסכים אתו למזבח, ואשם לכהנים, וצריך אשם אחר להכשירו:
Rashi on Menachot 89b:15:3.english: You have disqualified it - From being offered upon the altar: For it is not fit for the leper, since it was slaughtered not for its designated purpose; and it is not fit for a burnt-offering, since it was not relegated to grazing, and it is not fit for a voluntary offering, for a guilt-offering does not come as a voluntary offering. But the libations come to the altar, and the guilt-offering [goes] to the priests, and he requires another guilt-offering to qualify him.

Rashi on Menachot 89b:16:1.hebrew: כבש הבא עם העומר - דומיא דאשם מצורע, דכי היכי דאשם מצורע טעון נסכים ואין שאר אשמות טעונין נסכים, כך כבש הבא עם העומר נשתנית מנחתו משאר מנחות כבשים, דאילו שאר כבשים אין טעונין אלא עשרון וזה טעון ב' עשרונות. להכי נקט כבש הבא עם העומר:
Rashi on Menachot 89b:16:1.english: The lamb brought with the omer - [It is] analogous to the guilt-offering of a leper: For just as the guilt-offering of a leper requires libations whereas other guilt-offerings do not require libations, so too, the lamb brought with the omer differs in its meal-offering from the meal-offerings of other lambs; for while other lambs require only one-tenth [of an ephah], this one requires two-tenths. That is why [Rav Menashya bar Gada] specified the lamb brought with the omer.

Rashi on Menachot 89b:17:1.hebrew: תמיד של שחר יהא טעון ב' גזירין בכהן אחד - כדמפרש במסכת יומא (דף כו:): "ובער עליה הכהן עצים". אבל בין הערבים, ב' גזירין בב' כהנים, כדכתיב: "ובער וערכו":
Rashi on Menachot 89b:17:1.english: The morning daily offering requires two logs [brought] by one priest - As is explained in Tractate Yoma (26b): "And the priest shall kindle wood upon it." But [for the daily offering] of the afternoon, two logs [are brought] by two priests, as it is written: "And he shall kindle" [and] "and they shall arrange."

Rashi on Menachot 89b:18:1.hebrew: אין הכי נמי - דצריך למיעבד להו דינייהו כאילו נשחטו לשמן, כמו אשם מצורע:
Rashi on Menachot 89b:18:1.english: Yes, it is indeed so - That one must perform their procedures for them as if they were slaughtered for their own sake, just like the guilt-offering of a leper.

Rashi on Menachot 89b:18:2.hebrew: אלא אמר אביי - הא דלא אמרי אלא באשם מצורע, חדא מינייהו נקט:
Rashi on Menachot 89b:18:2.english: Rather, Abaye said - As for the fact that he stated [this] only regarding the guilt-offering of a metzora, he took one of them [as an example].

Rashi on Menachot 89b:19:1.hebrew: בשלמא הנך - כבשים דעומר ותמיד ששחטן שלא לשמן, לעולם אימא לך דלא צריכי הלכתייהו כדמעיקרא, לא גזירין ולא מנחה כפולה, ואפילו הכי לא מיפסלו למיקרב למזבח, משום דעולות נינהו, ואי לא חזו כו':
Rashi on Menachot 89b:19:1.english: Granted, those - Regarding the lambs of the omer and the daily offering [tamid] that were slaughtered not for their designated purpose [shelo lishman], I could always tell you that they do not require their original specific rules — neither [the logs of] wood nor the doubled meal offering — and even so, they are not disqualified from being offered upon the altar, because they are burnt offerings, and "if they are not fit [for this, they are fit for that]..."

Rashi on Menachot 89b:1:1.hebrew: וכן נמי מערבין נסכי כבשים של היום בנסכי כבשים של אמש, כדאמרינן (לעיל מנחות דף טו:) מביא אדם זבחו היום ונסכיו מכאן עד י' ימים:
Rashi on Menachot 89b:1:1.english: And similarly one may mix the libations of lambs of today with the libations of lambs of yesterday, as we said (above, Menachot 15b): a person may bring his sacrifice today and its libations from now until ten days [later].

Rashi on Menachot 89b:2:1.english: But one may not mix, etc. - Because these have a soft dough [consistency] while those have a thick dough [consistency].

Rashi on Menachot 89b:2:2.hebrew: בללן - לנסכי פרים בפני עצמן ולנסכי כבשים בפני עצמן, ושוב נתערבו כשרין. ואם נתערבו עד שלא בלל, פסולה:
Rashi on Menachot 89b:2:2.english: He mixed them - [He mixed] the libations of the bulls by themselves and the libations of the lambs by themselves, and then [if] they became intermingled, they are valid. But if they became intermingled before he had mixed [them], it is invalid.

Rashi on Menachot 89b:5:1.english: That one should not mix fats - So too, one should not mix libations [with libations of a different animal].

Rashi on Menachot 89b:6:1.hebrew: אמר רבי יוחנן - לא תימא מערבין לכתחלה, אלא אם נתערבו קאמר, והא דקתני והקטירו שלא יערב לכתחלה מיירי:
Rashi on Menachot 89b:6:1.english: Rabbi Yochanan said - Do not say that [the Mishnah permits] mixing ab initio; rather, [Rabbi Yochanan] is saying [that it speaks of a case] where they became mixed [after the fact]. And that which [the Mishnah] teaches, "and they shall burn them" — this deals with [the requirement] not to mix ab initio.

Rashi on Menachot 89b:7:1.english: If so - [the clause] that the Mishnah teaches, "but one may not mix the libations of lambs with the libations of bulls," [would mean] that even if they became mixed, after the fact it is also not [valid].

Rashi on Menachot 89b:7:2.english: But since the latter clause teaches "if they became mixed they are valid" - This means [the ruling applies only] after the fact.

Rashi on Menachot 89b:7:3.hebrew: מכלל דרישא אין מערבין לכתחלה - וה"ה רישא דרישא נמי מערבין לכתחלה, והדר קשיא לדוכתי' שלא יערב חלבים בחלבים:
Rashi on Menachot 89b:7:3.english: By inference, the first clause [implies] one may not mix ab initio - And the same law applies to the very beginning of the first clause: one may also mix ab initio. And thus the difficulty returns to its place — that one should not mix fats with fats.

Rashi on Menachot 89b:8:1.hebrew: אמר אביי - ודאי רישא דמתניתין דתני מערבין לכתחילה היא, ולא תיקשי לך, דנתערבו נסכים דמתני' ביינות קמיירי, והכי קאמר: מערבין יינן של נסכים פרים ואילים לכתחלה, אם נתערב כבר סלתן ושמנן מאיליהן, הואיל והתחיל לערב ליכא משום לא יערב חלבים, והא דתני אבל אין מערבין נסכי כבשים בנסכי פרים אפי' היכא דנתערב סלתן ושמנן:
Rashi on Menachot 89b:8:1.english: Abaye said - Certainly the first clause of our Mishnah teaches that one may mix ab initio, and it should present no difficulty for you: for when the Mishnah speaks of libations that became mixed, it is referring to the wine. And this is what it is saying: one may mix the wine of the libations of bulls and rams ab initio; and if their flour and oil have already become mixed on their own, since mixing has already begun there is no violation of the prohibition against mixing fats. And what the Mishnah teaches — "but one may not mix the libations of lambs with the libations of bulls" — applies even where their flour and oil have become mixed.

Rashi on Menachot 89b:9:1.hebrew: ויין לכתחלה לא - אפי' דאילים ופרים אם לא נתערב סלתן ושמנן. והא תניא בד"א דאין מערבין נסכי כבשים בנסכי פרים ואילים בסלת ושמן, אבל יין מערבין לכתחילה בין נתערב סלתו ושמנו בין לא נתערב:
Rashi on Menachot 89b:9:1.english: And wine, ab initio, no — Even for rams and bulls, if their flour and oil have not been mixed [with those of lambs]. But the baraita teaches: "In what case" does one not mix the libations of lambs with those of bulls and rams? [Only regarding] flour and oil — but wine one may mix ab initio, whether their flour and oil have already been mixed or have not been mixed.

Tosafot on Menachot 89b:15:1.hebrew: שאם אי אתה אומר כן פסלתו - תימה, אם כן, כבשי עצרת ששחטן שלא לשמן, דתניא בפ' התכלת (לעיל מנחות מח.): "הדם יזרק והבשר יאכל" — אמאי? הא כיון דבעי לחם ולא קדש הלחם, יפסל! וכן תודה ששחטה שלא לשמה, תיפסל, כיון דלא קדש הלחם! ושלמי נזיר ששחטן שלא כמצותן, דקאמר דאין טעונין לא לחם ולא זרוע; וכן מפריש מעות לנזירותו ומת, דאמר בפ' קמא (לעיל מנחות ד:): דמי שלמים יביא בהן שלמים, ואין טעונים לחם. ולרבא ניחא, דמשני: בשלמא הנך עולות נינהו, אי לא חזו לעולת חובה חזו לעולת נדבה, הכא נמי שלמים נינהו, אי לא חזו לשלמי חובה חזו לשלמי נדבה; אלא לאביי קשיא. ואפי' לרבא נמי קשה, דהא ציבור לא מייתו שלמי נדבה! ויש לומר, דלחם לא דמי לנסכים, דנסכים חשיבי טפי כגוף הקרבן משום דקרבי למזבח, אבל לחם לא חשיב כגוף הקרבן משום דאין בו למזבח. וזרוע בשילה נמי, אף על גב דגופא דזיבחא הוא, אין לחוש בכך, דשלמי נזיר גופייהו, אפי' לא היה מקיים בהן מצות זרוע בשילה, לא היו פסולין בכך, הואיל ונעשו העבודות כמצותן:
Tosafot on Menachot 89b:15:1.english: For if you do not say so, you have disqualified it - This is difficult: If so, regarding the lambs of Atzeret [Shavuot] that were slaughtered not for their own sake [shelo lishman], concerning which it is taught in the chapter "HaTekhelet" (above, 48a): "The blood shall be sprinkled and the flesh may be eaten" — why? Since they require bread, and the bread was not consecrated, [the offering] should be disqualified! And similarly, a thanks-offering slaughtered not for its own sake [shelo lishmah] should be disqualified, since the bread was not consecrated! And [likewise with] the peace-offerings of a nazirite that were slaughtered not in their prescribed manner, where [the Gemara] states that they require neither bread nor the cooked foreleg; and likewise one who sets aside money for his naziriteship and dies, where [the Gemara] said in the first chapter (above, 4b): with the money for peace-offerings he brings peace-offerings, and they do not require bread. Now, according to Rava this is fine, as he answers [below, 90a]: Granted, those are burnt-offerings; if they are not fit for an obligatory burnt-offering, they are fit for a voluntary burnt-offering. Here too, they are peace-offerings; if they are not fit for an obligatory peace-offering, they are fit for a voluntary peace-offering. [Since voluntary peace-offerings do not require bread, omitting it does not disqualify them.] But according to Abaye, it is difficult. And even according to Rava it is also difficult, for the community does not bring voluntary peace-offerings [so the communal Shavuot lambs cannot be categorized as voluntary peace-offerings]! And it can be answered that bread is not comparable to libations. For libations are considered more like the body of the sacrifice itself, because they are offered upon the altar; but bread is not considered like the body of the sacrifice, because none of it goes to the altar. And regarding the cooked foreleg as well, even though it is [part of] the body of the sacrifice itself, there is no need to be concerned about this, because with the nazirite's peace-offerings themselves, even if one did not fulfill the mitzvah of the cooked foreleg with them, they would not be disqualified thereby, since the [essential] sacrificial services were performed according to their commandment.

Tosafot on Menachot 89b:17:1.hebrew: תמיד של שחר טעון שני גזירין - בכהן אחד אחר סידור כל המערכה, ושל בין הערבים בשני כהנים ושני גזירין, כדמפרש בפרק ב' דמסכת יומא (דף כו:), כך פירש בקונטרס. והכי תנן התם בפרק ב' (ג"ז שם): דתמיד קרב בתשעה, בעשרה, באחד עשר, לא פחות ולא יותר. עצמו בתשעה; בחג, ביד אחד צלוחית של מים, הרי כאן עשרה; בין הערבים בי"א: עצמו בתשעה, ושנים בידן שני גזירי עצים. והשתא תימה: אי גזירי עצים דתמיד של שחר בכהן אחד, הוה ליה עצמו בעשרה, או באחד עשר אי טעונים שני כהנים! וצריך לומר, דלא חשיבא שני גזירין של שחרית משום דלפני שחיטת תמיד השחר הן משכימין לסדר המערכה, לא חשיב אלא העוסקין בשעת התמיד; דסידור שני גזירין היה אפילו קודם תרומת הדשן, כדאיתא בסידור המערכה דאביי בפרק אמר להן הממונה (יומא דף לג.). והיינו דאמר בירושלמי בפ"ב דיומא: אמר רבי יוחנן: לא גזרו על שני גזירין בשחרית (פי' שיהו בשעת הקטרת איברים). א"ר אסי: מתניתין אמרה כן, בכל יום קרב בין הערבים באחד עשר, ולא אמר בשחרית כלום. ומהשתא ליכא למידק מהתם כלל אי הויא בכהן אחד או בשני כהנים. ומיהו יש לדקדק מהא דתניא התם בגמ' ביומא (דף כו:): מנין לתמיד של בין הערבים שטעון שני גזירין בשני כהנים? שנאמר: "וערכו עצים על האש", אם אינו ענין לתמיד של שחר, שנאמר: "ובער עליה הכהן עצים בבקר", תניהו ענין לתמיד של בין הערבים; ואימא אידי ואידי בתמיד של שחר, וקאמר רחמנא ניעבד בחד והדר נעביד בתרי! אלמא משמע בהדיא דשל שחר בחד, משום דכתיב "וביער" לשון יחיד, ושל בין הערבים בתרי, משום דכתיב "וערכו" לשון רבים. ועוד תניא התם (דף כז:) בסוף פירקא: מי שזכה בתרומת הדשן יזכה בסידור מערכה ובשני גזירי עצים:
Tosafot on Menachot 89b:17:1.english: The morning daily-offering requires two logs - [Brought] by one priest after arranging the entire pyre, and that of the afternoon [is brought] by two priests and two logs, as is explained in chapter 2 of tractate Yoma (26b). So Rashi explained. And so we learned there in chapter 2 (ibid.): The daily-offering was sacrificed by nine, by ten, or by eleven [priests], no fewer and no more. The offering itself was sacrificed by nine; on the festival [of Sukkot], when one held a flask of water in his hand [for the water libation], there were ten; in the afternoon by eleven: the offering itself by nine, and two holding two logs of wood in their hands. Now this is difficult: if the logs of wood for the morning daily-offering are [brought] by one priest, the offering itself should have been [offered] by ten — or by eleven if they require two priests! And one must say that the two logs of the morning are not counted because they rise early to arrange the pyre before the slaughter of the morning daily-offering, [and the Mishnah] counts only those who are engaged [in the service] at the time of the daily-offering. For the arrangement of the two logs took place even before the removal of the ashes, as is stated in Abaye's [ordering of] the arrangement of the pyres in the chapter "Amar Lahem HaMemonah" (Yoma 33a). And this is what is said in the Yerushalmi in chapter 2 of Yoma: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: They did not decree concerning the two logs in the morning — meaning, that they should be [brought] at the time of burning the limbs. Rabbi Assi said: The Mishnah also says this: "Every day it was sacrificed in the afternoon by eleven," and it did not say anything [about wood] in the morning. Now from this, there is no inference to be drawn at all as to whether it was [done] by one priest or by two priests. However, one can deduce [that the morning logs were brought by one priest] from that which is taught there in the Gemara in Yoma (26b): From where is it derived that the afternoon daily-offering requires two logs [brought] by two priests? As it is stated: "And [the sons of Aaron the priest] shall lay wood in order upon the fire" (Leviticus 1:7). If this is not relevant to the morning daily-offering, of which it is stated: "And the priest shall kindle wood upon it every morning" (Leviticus 6:5), apply it as relevant to the afternoon daily-offering. [And the Gemara suggests:] But say that both this and that [verse apply] to the morning daily-offering, and the Torah says: let it be done by one, and then let it be done by two! From this, it explicitly implies that that of the morning is by one, because it is written: "And [the priest] shall kindle" — in the singular; and that of the afternoon is by two, because it is written: "And they shall lay in order" — in the plural. Furthermore, it is taught there (27a) at the end of the chapter: The one who won [the lottery for] the removal of the ashes would win the arrangement of the pyre and the two logs of wood.

Tosafot on Menachot 89b:2:1.english: If one mixed these on their own and those on their own [and they became intermingled, they are] valid - [This follows] the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Yehuda in [the chapter of] HaKometz Rabba (above, Menachot 23a), who say that a dry [meal-offering] that became mixed with an oil-mixed one may be offered.

Tosafot on Menachot 89b:2:2.english: And if before he mixed [the oil in], they became mixed with invalid [offerings], they are invalid - because we require [the offering] to be fit for mixing.

Tosafot on Menachot 89b:7:1.hebrew: והא מדקתני סיפא בללן אלו בפני עצמן כו' - תימה, מאי קשיא? דלעולם אין מערבין, אפי' נתערבו נמי לא, וכגון שלא בלל. ונראה דלא מייתי ההוא דאין מערבין אלא משום דסיפא דבללן אלו בפני עצמן כו' עלה קאי אנסכי כבשים בנסכי פרים ואילים, אבל לא דייק כלל אלא מהא דמדקתני סיפא ונתערבו בלשון דיעבד, מכלל דמערבין דרישא לכתחילה קאמר:
Tosafot on Menachot 89b:7:1.english: But from the fact that the latter clause teaches, "they mixed these by themselves," etc. - This is difficult: what is the difficulty? For one could always say that one may never mix them, and even if they became mixed, they are still invalid - and the case is one where he did not blend them. And it seems that the ruling "one may not mix" is cited only because the latter clause - "they mixed these by themselves," etc. - bears upon the case of the libations of lambs mixed with the libations of bulls and rams. But the actual inference is drawn not from there at all, but rather from the fact that the latter clause teaches the case of "they became mixed" in the language of after-the-fact (bedieved) - which implies by inference that the first clause's "one mixes" is speaking of the outset (lekhatchilah).
